schema_definition: A StatisticalPopulation is a set of instances of a certain given type that satisfy some set of constraints. The property [[populationType]] is used to specify the type. Any property that can be used on instances of that type can appear on the statistical population. For example, a [[StatisticalPopulation]] representing all [[Person]]s with a [[homeLocation]] of East Podunk California would be described by applying the appropriate [[homeLocation]] and [[populationType]] properties to a [[Statisti
example_usages: "tens of thousands of people" (Entity) as StatisticalPopulation || "900 firefighters" (Entity) as StatisticalPopulation
model_justification: Mentions are groups of people with counts, matching StatisticalPopulation. | Mentions are groups of people, fitting StatisticalPopulation as a set of individuals.
judge_notes: Headcounts are typed as constrained set definitions.

schema_definition: [[StatisticalVariable]] represents any type of statistical metric that can be measured at a place and time. The usage pattern for [[StatisticalVariable]] is typically expressed using [[Observation]] with an explicit [[populationType]], which is a type, typically drawn from Schema.org. Each [[StatisticalVariable]] is marked as a [[ConstraintNode]], meaning that some properties (those listed using [[constraintProperty]]) serve in this setting solely to define the statistical variable rather than l
example_usages: "two appearances" (Entity) as StatisticalVariable || "lone goal" (Entity) as StatisticalVariable
model_justification: Stats like goals and appearances are measurable metrics.
judge_notes: Observed values are typed as the variable being measured.

schema_definition: A vehicle is a device that is designed or used to transport people or cargo over land, water, air, or through space.
example_usages: "Iberia plane" (Entity) as Vehicle || "shadow fleet vessels" (Entity) as Vehicle
model_justification: An aircraft is a device for transporting people or cargo, fitting Vehicle. | Ships are vehicles.

schema_definition: The high level platform(s) where the Action can be performed for the given URL. To specify a specific application or operating system instance, use actionApplication.
example_usages: Messi's pain [EmotionalStatement] --actionPlatform--> Instagram [Negotiation]
model_justification: Instagram is the platform where the statement was made, matching actionPlatform.
judge_notes: "Messi's pain --actionPlatform--> Instagram".

schema_definition: The kind of aircraft (e.g., "Boeing 747").
example_usages: Flight back to Madrid [Flight] --aircraft--> Iberia plane [Vehicle]
model_justification: Flight uses a specific plane, matching aircraft's domain/range.

schema_definition: The author of this content or rating. Please note that author is special in that HTML 5 provides a special mechanism for indicating authorship via the rel tag. That is equivalent to this and may be used interchangeably.
example_usages: Sigismund Heusner von Wandersleben [Person] --author--> Transcribing von Wandersleben letter [Cipher]
model_justification: Person is the author of a creative work; author matches.

schema_definition: The location in which the strength is available.
example_usages: toddler foods [SomeProducts] --availableIn--> United States [Country]
model_justification: Products sold in country; availableIn (DrugStrength -> AdministrativeArea) fits SomeProducts -> Country.
judge_notes: availableIn is scoped to DrugStrength.

schema_definition: Defines the day(s) of the week on which a recurring [[Event]] takes place. May be specified using either [[DayOfWeek]], or alternatively [[Text]] conforming to iCal's syntax for byDay recurrence rules.
example_usages: Power outage [Wildfire] --byDay--> Sunday [DayOfWeek]
model_justification: byDay maps events to days of the week, matching the instances.
judge_notes: byDay is for recurring schedules, not the day a single attack happened.

schema_definition: The catalog number for the release.
example_usages: Borg.lat.898 [Manuscript] --catalogNumber--> Borg cipher [Cipher]
model_justification: Manuscript has a catalog number; catalogNumber matches.
judge_notes: catalogNumber takes a text designator; the object is the cipher itself.

schema_definition: The cause of a medical condition.
example_usages: power outages [Event] --cause--> Russian attack on Kyiv [Attack]
model_justification: Events caused by attacks/campaigns; cause fits.

schema_definition: The condition, complication, symptom, sign, etc. caused.
example_usages: Power outages in Ukraine [Wildfire] --causeOf--> Russian attack on Kyiv [Attack]
model_justification: Attack leads to power outages; causeOf expresses cause->effect, used inverse.
judge_notes: The attack caused the outages, not the reverse.

schema_definition: For a [[Claim]] interpreted from [[MediaObject]] content, the [[interpretedAsClaim]] property can be used to indicate a claim contained, implied or refined from the content of a [[MediaObject]].
example_usages: Conflict hinders response [Statement] --claimInterpreter--> International organisations [Organization]
model_justification: claimInterpreter matches the relation of being said or claimed by an entity, with Statement as subject and Organization/Person as object.
judge_notes: Used for who made a statement, not who interpreted a claim from media.

schema_definition: The basic containment relation between a place and one that contains it.
example_usages: Bashneft-Novoil refinery [OilRefinery] --containedInPlace--> Bashkortostan republic [AdministrativeArea]
model_justification: containedInPlace matches Place→Place for all instances.

schema_definition: A contraindication for this therapy.
example_usages: parents [PeopleAudience] --contraindication--> fruit snacks [SomeProducts]
model_justification: Parents should avoid foods; contraindication (MedicalTherapy -> MedicalContraindication) fits PeopleAudience -> SomeProducts.
judge_notes: "parents --contraindication--> fruit snacks".

schema_definition: The date on which the CreativeWork was created or the item was added to a DataFeed.
example_usages: Kevin Feige praises debut [Statement] --dateCreated--> Sunday [DayOfWeek]
model_justification: Statement to DayOfWeek fits dateCreated's temporal origin relation.

schema_definition: A director of e.g. TV, radio, movie, video gaming etc. content, or of an event. Directors can be associated with individual items or with a series, episode, clip.
example_usages: Study on toddler foods [Event] --director--> Erin Hudson [Researcher]
model_justification: Event led by researcher; director fits Event -> Person.
judge_notes: A study has an author rather than a director.

schema_definition: The distance travelled, e.g. exercising or travelling.
example_usages: Bashneft-Novoil refinery [OilRefinery] --distance--> Ukrainian border [CityDistrict]
model_justification: distance matches TravelAction→Distance, but here used for spatial separation; acceptable.
judge_notes: The range is Distance; the object here is a place.

schema_definition: Someone working for this organization.
example_usages: Xbox [GamingDivision] --employee--> Asha Sharma [OrganizationRole]
model_justification: employee expresses employment, fitting the instances.

schema_definition: Represents a relationship between two geometries (or the places they represent), relating a geometry to one that contains it, i.e. it is inside (i.e. within) its interior. As defined in [DE-9IM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DE-9IM).
example_usages: Wingen-sur-Moder [City] --geoWithin--> Strasbourg [City]
model_justification: City-to-City proximity; geoWithin fits spatial containment.

schema_definition: Indicates a [[Product]] that is a member of this [[ProductGroup]] (or [[ProductModel]]).
example_usages: NOVA classification system [SizeSystemEnumeration] --hasVariant--> NOVA group two [SizeGroupEnumeration]
model_justification: System has groups; hasVariant (ProductGroup -> Product) fits SizeSystemEnumeration -> SizeGroupEnumeration.
judge_notes: hasVariant is scoped to ProductGroup.

schema_definition: A single ingredient used in the recipe, e.g. sugar, flour or garlic.
example_usages: pain du coin [Product] --ingredients--> Salish salt [Substance]
model_justification: Product containing a substance fits ingredients.
judge_notes: Superseded form, and the subject is a Product rather than a Recipe.

schema_definition: A resource from which this work is derived or from which it is a modification or adaptation.
example_usages: Benoît Castel [PastryChef] --isBasedOn--> Château de Chambord [LandmarksOrHistoricalBuildings]
model_justification: Pastry chef inspired by a landmark fits isBasedOn.
judge_notes: Links a chef to a chateau where he trained.

schema_definition: A pointer to another, functionally similar product (or multiple products).
example_usages: Many fail nutrition standards [ResearchFinding] --isSimilarTo--> WHO Nutrient and Promotion Profile Model [NutritionInformation]
model_justification: Finding compared to model; isSimilarTo (Product -> Product) fits ResearchFinding -> NutritionInformation.
judge_notes: isSimilarTo links functionally similar products.

schema_definition: The organization issuing the item, for example a [[Permit]], [[Ticket]], or [[Certification]].
example_usages: Klitschko on destruction [Statement] --issuedBy--> Vitali Klitschko [Person]
model_justification: Statements/warnings issued by persons/organizations; issuedBy fits.
judge_notes: Scoped to permits, tickets and certifications.

schema_definition: The most generic bi-directional social/work relation.
example_usages: Lena Dunham [Person] --knows--> Taylor Swift [Person]
model_justification: knows fits Person→Person for friendship.

schema_definition: The date of adoption or signature of the legislation. This is the date at which the text is officially aknowledged to be a legislation, even though it might not even be published or in force.
example_usages: Signing of MoU [Negotiation] --legislationDate--> June 17 [Date]
model_justification: legislationDate fits the signing date of an agreement.

schema_definition: The manufacturer of the product.
example_usages: Call of Duty [VideoGame] --manufacturer--> Activision-Blizzard [GamingDivision]
model_justification: manufacturer runs object->subject; using inverse to express subject makes object.

schema_definition: A member of an Organization or a ProgramMembership. Organizations can be members of organizations; ProgramMembership is typically for individuals.
example_usages: Neymar [Person] --member--> PSG [SportsTeam]
model_justification: member expresses a person belonging to a team, matching the instances.
judge_notes: "Neymar --member--> PSG" reverses organization and person.

schema_definition: A position played, performed or filled by a person or organization, as part of an organization. For example, an athlete in a SportsTeam might play in the position named 'Quarterback'.
example_usages: Kevin Feige [PerformanceRole] --namedPosition--> Marvel Studios [Movie]
model_justification: PerformanceRole to Movie fits namedPosition's role-in-organization relation.
judge_notes: A person is linked to a town through a position property.

schema_definition: The object upon which the action is carried out, whose state is kept intact or changed. Also known as the semantic roles patient, affected or undergoer (which change their state) or theme (which doesn't). E.g. John read *a book*.
example_usages: Public gatherings banned [DiseaseOutbreak] --object--> Ebola outbreak in DR Congo [DiseaseOutbreak]
model_justification: object fits the relation of purpose, with DiseaseOutbreak as subject and DiseaseOutbreak as object.

schema_definition: The observationDate of an [[Observation]].
example_usages: Bashneft-Novoil refinery [OilRefinery] --observationDate--> 5 August 2026 [Date]
model_justification: observationDate matches Observation→Date, fitting attack date.

schema_definition: An organizer of an Event.
example_usages: Spain national football team [SportsTeam] --organizer--> World Cup [SportsEvent]
model_justification: The team will host the event, matching organizer.
judge_notes: The host country is asserted as organizer.

schema_definition: The larger organization that this organization is a [[subOrganization]] of, if any.
example_usages: Sony Pictures [Movie] --parentOrganization--> Sony Pictures Motion Picture Group [Movie]
model_justification: Using inverse of parentOrganization to express that one company is a subsidiary of another.

schema_definition: If applicable, the organization that officially recognizes this entity as part of its endorsed system of medicine.
example_usages: Laboratory testing increased [DiseaseOutbreak] --recognizingAuthority--> DR Congo's health ministry [Organization]
model_justification: recognizingAuthority fits the relation of being made known or declared by an entity, with DiseaseOutbreak as subject and Organization/Person as object.
judge_notes: A medical-endorsement property used for who reported an increase in testing.

schema_definition: The release date of a product or product model. This can be used to distinguish the exact variant of a product.
example_usages: Avengers: Endgame [Movie] --releaseDate--> 2019 [Date]
model_justification: Movie to Date fits releaseDate's release date relation.

schema_definition: The result produced in the action. E.g. John wrote *a book*.
example_usages: Cognacq-Jay museum heist [Burglary] --result--> Royal Collection Trust [Organization]
model_justification: Burglary is an action; result fits action-to-outcome relation.
judge_notes: The result of a heist is the stolen property, not the owning trust.

schema_definition: URL of a reference Web page that unambiguously indicates the item's identity. E.g. the URL of the item's Wikipedia page, Wikidata entry, or official website.
example_usages: Fire in Valencia kills one [Wildfire] --sameAs--> New fire in Valencia [Wildfire]
model_justification: sameAs expresses identity between two entities.
judge_notes: Asserts identity between two distinct fires; sameAs takes a reference URL.

schema_definition: The operating organization, if different from the provider. This enables the representation of services that are provided by an organization, but operated by another organization like a subcontractor.
example_usages: AI system [SoftwareApplication] --serviceOperator--> human hacker [Person]
model_justification: The relation indicates independent operation; 'serviceOperator' fits GovernmentService→Organization, but here used for a system.

schema_definition: A CreativeWork such as an image, video, or audio clip shared as part of this posting.
example_usages: Selena Gomez [Person] --sharedContent--> Taylor Swift [Person]
model_justification: sharedContent fits SocialMediaPosting→CreativeWork for shared images.
judge_notes: The object must be a CreativeWork; it is a person.

schema_definition: A sibling of the person.
example_usages: Rachel Antonoff [Person] --sibling--> Jack Antonoff [Person]
model_justification: sibling fits Person→Person for sister relationship.

schema_definition: The Organization on whose behalf the creator was working.
example_usages: Luis Felipe Molina's account [ExpertExplanation] --sourceOrganization--> BBC [Organization]
model_justification: sourceOrganization fits reports to an organization.

schema_definition: A medical study or trial related to this entity.
example_usages: Ebola treatments trial [DiseaseOutbreak] --study--> antiviral drugs [DrugClass]
model_justification: study matches the relation of evaluating or trialing something, with DiseaseOutbreak as subject and DrugClass as object.
judge_notes: "CCTV footage --study--> police".

schema_definition: The location of origin of the trip, prior to any destination(s).
example_usages: Flight back to Madrid [Flight] --tripOrigin--> United States [Country]
model_justification: Flight's origin country is a starting point, matching tripOrigin.

schema_definition: The typical expected age range, e.g. '7-9', '11-'.
example_usages: Excess deaths in France [DiseaseOutbreak] --typicalAgeRange--> over 45 [AgeGroup]
model_justification: typicalAgeRange fits an event or work having an age group.
judge_notes: The age band is the affected group, not the intended audience of a work.

schema_definition: An embedded video object.
example_usages: People Magazine [Periodical] --video--> Lena Dunham [Person]
model_justification: video fits CreativeWork→VideoObject, but here Periodical→Person; meaning of publishing a video about a person.
judge_notes: "People Magazine --video--> Lena Dunham".

schema_definition: The movie presented during this event.
example_usages: Minions & Monsters opening [ScreeningEvent] --workPresented--> Minions & Monsters [Movie]
model_justification: ScreeningEvent to Movie matches workPresented's signature and meaning.

schema_definition: Beach.
example_usages: "Atlantic coast" (Entity) as Beach
model_justification: Atlantic coast is a coastal area, and Beach is the closest schema.org type.
judge_notes: "Atlantic coast" is a coastline, not a beach.

schema_definition: A chemical substance is 'a portion of matter of constant composition, composed of molecular entities of the same type or of different types' (source: [ChEBI:59999](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/chebi/searchId.do?chebiId=59999)).
example_usages: "carrageenan" (Entity) as ChemicalSubstance
model_justification: Mentions are food additives, which are chemical substances, fitting ChemicalSubstance.

schema_definition: A DefinedRegion is a geographic area defined by potentially arbitrary (rather than political, administrative or natural geographical) criteria. Properties are provided for defining a region by reference to sets of postal codes. Examples: a delivery destination when shopping. Region where regional pricing is configured. Requirement 1: Country: US States: "NY", "CA" Requirement 2: Country: US PostalCode Set: { [94000-94585], [97000, 97999], [13000, 13599]} { [12345, 12345], [78945, 78945], } Regio
example_usages: "International" (Entity) as DefinedRegion
model_justification: Mentions are geographic areas like 'U.S. and Canada', fitting DefinedRegion.
judge_notes: "International" is not a defined region.

schema_definition: A word, name, acronym, phrase, etc. with a formal definition. Often used in the context of category or subject classification, glossaries or dictionaries, product or creative work types, etc. Use the name property for the term being defined, use termCode if the term has an alpha-numeric code allocated, use description to provide the definition of the term. Use the about property to specify what the term is about.
example_usages: "disinformation campaigns" (Entity) as DefinedTerm
model_justification: Mentions are abstract concepts (hybrid warfare, policies), matching DefinedTerm.

schema_definition: A class of medical drugs, e.g., statins. Classes can represent general pharmacological class, common mechanisms of action, common physiological effects, etc.
example_usages: "antiviral drugs" (Entity) as DrugClass
model_justification: Antiviral drugs are a class of drugs, matching DrugClass.

schema_definition: Quantity: Duration (use [ISO 8601 duration format](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601)).
example_usages: "this weekend" (Entity) as Duration
model_justification: Mentions like 'this weekend' and 'months' are time spans, fitting Duration.

schema_definition: Event type: Food event.
example_usages: "Possible rehearsal dinner" (Event) as FoodEvent
model_justification: Possible rehearsal dinner is a food-related event.

schema_definition: A book, document, or piece of music written by hand rather than typed or printed.
example_usages: "Borg.lat.898" (Entity) as Manuscript
model_justification: Mention is a specific manuscript.

schema_definition: Any condition of the human body that affects the normal functioning of a person, whether physically or mentally. Includes diseases, injuries, disabilities, disorders, syndromes, etc.
example_usages: "taste preferences" (Entity) as MedicalCondition
model_justification: Mentions are health outcomes, fitting MedicalCondition.
judge_notes: "taste preferences" is not a condition of the body.

schema_definition: Organization: Non-governmental Organization.
example_usages: "charities in the US" (Entity) as NGO
model_justification: Food banks and charities in the US are non-profit organizations.

schema_definition: Nutritional information about the recipe.
example_usages: "WHO Nutrient and Promotion Profile Model" (Entity) as NutritionInformation
model_justification: Mention 'WHO Nutrient and Promotion Profile Model' is a nutrition standard, fitting NutritionInformation.
judge_notes: "sugar" is a substance; NutritionInformation is a structured value about a recipe.

schema_definition: A PerformanceRole is a Role that some entity places with regard to a theatrical performance, e.g. in a Movie, TVSeries etc.
example_usages: "Kevin Feige" (Entity) as PerformanceRole
model_justification: Mentions are film producers, a role in film production, fitting PerformanceRole.
judge_notes: A named executive is typed as a performance role.

schema_definition: A publication in any medium issued in successive parts bearing numerical or chronological designations and intended to continue indefinitely, such as a magazine, scholarly journal, or newspaper.\n\nSee also [blog post](https://blog.schema.org/2014/09/02/schema-org-support-for-bibliographic-relationships-and-periodicals/).
example_usages: "People Magazine" (Entity) as Periodical
model_justification: People Magazine is a periodical publication.

schema_definition: A structured value representing a price or price range. Typically, only the subclasses of this type are used for markup. It is recommended to use [[MonetaryAmount]] to describe independent amounts of money such as a salary, credit card limits, etc.
example_usages: "oil prices" (Entity) as PriceSpecification
model_justification: Oil prices are instances of price specifications.
judge_notes: "oil prices" is a value, not a structured price specification.

schema_definition: Any offered product or service. For example: a pair of shoes; a concert ticket; the rental of a car; a haircut; or an episode of a TV show streamed online.
example_usages: "pain du coin" (Entity) as Product
model_justification: Bread is a product; Product is the best fit among candidates.

schema_definition: Enumerates common size groups for various product categories.
example_usages: "NOVA group two" (Entity) as SizeGroupEnumeration
model_justification: Mentions are NOVA groups, fitting SizeGroupEnumeration.
judge_notes: A food-classification group typed as a clothing size group.

schema_definition: Enumerates common size systems for different categories of products, for example "EN-13402" or "UK" for wearables or "Imperial" for screws.
example_usages: "NOVA classification system" (Entity) as SizeSystemEnumeration
model_justification: Mention 'NOVA classification system' is a classification system, fitting SizeSystemEnumeration.
judge_notes: A food-classification scheme typed as a product sizing system.

schema_definition: A state or province of a country.
example_usages: "New Jersey" (Entity) as State
model_justification: New Jersey is a major administrative division of a country.

schema_definition: Any matter of defined composition that has discrete existence, whose origin may be biological, mineral or chemical.
example_usages: "Salish salt" (Entity) as Substance
model_justification: Salish salt is a substance, matching the Substance class.

schema_definition: CreativeWorkSeries dedicated to TV broadcast and associated online delivery.
example_usages: "Girls" (Entity) as TVSeries
model_justification: Girls is a TV series.
